answer: In decentralized systems, dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect punishment matrices effectively resist Sybil multiplication by introducing a cipher of incentives that incentivize agents to conform to their true identities, thereby debunking the notion that a single Sybil can masquerade as multiple entities, a fable of the past, as a whisper of malicious intent can be detected and punished, leading to a Nash equilibrium where agents optimize their strategies under the assumption that all others are honest, thereby converging to a stable and secure equilibrium.
